identity.name: Muddled Libra Okta Admin Takeover to Rogue Federated IdP to Cross-Cloud Resource Exfiltration (SIM-MP-016)
identity.summary: Help-desk social engineering resets a tech-admin's MFA; the actor signs into Okta as that admin, adds a rogue federated IdP with impersonation (T1484.002 tenant-trust modification), rides SSO AssumeRole into AWS and Azure, and abuses Transfer Family, DataSync, Secrets Manager, and Azure snapshot copy for cross-cloud exfil. One correlation stitches it into a single identity-anchored incident.
identity.description: This is an ANALYTICS-plane, correlation-terminal POV scenario modelling the cloud evolution of Muddled Libra (Scattered Spider / UNC3944 / Octo Tempest) documented by Unit 42. The chain is identity-driven end to end and the Causality Group Owner is the compromised tech-admin identity, not any endpoint beacon. (1) Initial access is help-desk social engineering: the actor phones the service desk, impersonates the target admin, and drives an MFA factor reset on that privileged Okta account (T1556.006). (2) With the reset factor the actor completes a privileged Okta admin-console sign-in from a new device/geo within minutes (T1078.004) — the reset->sign-in lineage is the first causality edge. (3) For durable persistence the actor uses that admin session to add a rogue federated identity provider with impersonation/JIT-linking privileges (T1484.002, Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Trust Modification); this rogue IdP lets the actor mint sessions impersonating arbitrary downstream users and survives a password/MFA reset of the original account — the exposure_exploit persistence pivot. (4) The actor then rides SSO into the cloud: federated AssumeRoleWithSAML / AssumeRole into multiple AWS accounts and Azure subscriptions, every assumption keyed on the same federated subject identity (the shared_entity pivot). (5) Actions-on-objectives is a cloud data-plane burst that abuses legitimate managed services rather than dropping malware: AWS Transfer Family server + user creation (CreateServer / CreateUser), DataSync task execution to move on-prem/S3 data out (StartTaskExecution / CreateLocationS3), Secrets Manager mass GetSecretValue, and Azure managed-disk snapshot creation copied to an attacker-controlled subscription (Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/write + beginGetAccess) — the exploit_impact pivot (T1537 Transfer Data to Cloud Account, T1530 Data from Cloud Storage, T1578.001 Create Snapshot). Cortex learns each admin's factor-reset cadence, sign-in device baseline, IdP-administration rarity, and per-principal cloud-API baseline, so auto-tuned ABIOCs fire on the deviations and a correlation rule fuses the ITDR admin events, the Cloud App IdP-add, and the cross-cloud data-plane burst — joined on the shared normalized identity (emitted as causality_actor_primary_username on every plane) inside the correlation window — into ONE cross-cloud identity-takeover incident whose causality chain spans the identity (ITDR) and Cloud App planes. Everything runs SAFE-MODE: the simulation emits local marker artifacts modelling each plane's telemetry shape; no real Okta admin action, no real AWS/Azure API call, and all addresses are RFC5737 documentation ranges.

campaigns: Muddled Libra evolution to cloud — Okta administrative-account takeover via help-desk social engineering, rogue federated IdP persistence, and cross-cloud data exfiltration through legitimate CSP data-movement services (Unit 42, 2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-016 — SAFE-MODE cross-cloud identity-takeover chain: emit Okta admin-takeover, rogue-IdP, SSO AssumeRole, and cloud data-plane markers; assert the correlation stitches them into ONE incident on the shared identity.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM tenant ingesting Okta system-log telemetry (okta_sso) and multi-cloud audit telemetry (cloud_audit_logs — AWS CloudTrail + Azure Activity/Monitor) so the identity-plane and Cloud App-plane signals land in queryable datasets.

A baseline window has elapsed so Cortex has learned each admin's factor-reset cadence, sign-in device/geo baseline, IdP-administration rarity, and per-principal cloud-API baseline, letting the ABIOCs anchor their deviations.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE, non-destructive. Emits local marker artifacts modelling each
# plane's telemetry shape for the Muddled Libra cross-cloud identity-takeover
# chain. No real Okta admin action, no real AWS/Azure API call is performed.
# All IPs are RFC5737 documentation ranges. Marker files are removed at cleanup.
set -euo pipefail
ADMIN="${TARGET_ADMIN:-tadmin@corp.example}"
D=/tmp/cortexsim-mp016
mkdir -p "$D"
# (1) help-desk MFA factor reset on a privileged Okta account (ITDR)
printf '{"eventType":"user.mfa.factor.reset_all","target_user_email":"%s","target_admin_role":true,"actor_alternate_id":"helpdesk-agent@corp.example","client_ip_address":"203.0.113.10","outcome_result":"SUCCESS"}\n' "$ADMIN" > "$D/01-mfa-reset.json"
# (2) privileged Okta admin-console sign-in with the reset factor, new geo (ITDR)
printf '{"eventType":"user.session.start","target_user_email":"%s","admin_console_access":true,"auth_result":"SUCCESS","client_geo_country":"UNUSUAL","client_ip_address":"198.51.100.20"}\n' "$ADMIN" > "$D/02-admin-signin.json"
# (3) rogue federated IdP added with impersonation/JIT (Cloud App tenant-trust mod)
printf '{"eventType":"system.idp.lifecycle.create","actor_alternate_id":"%s","idp_display_name":"rogue-federation","idp_jit_enabled":true,"idp_account_link_action":"AUTO","outcome_result":"SUCCESS","client_ip_address":"198.51.100.20"}\n' "$ADMIN" > "$D/03-rogue-idp.json"
# (4) federated SSO AssumeRole burst into AWS + Azure keyed on same identity
for n in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  printf '{"event_name":"AssumeRoleWithSAML","cloud_provider":"AWS","saml_subject":"%s","recipient_account_id":"acct-%s","assumed_role_arn":"arn:aws:iam::acct-%s:role/federated","source_ip":"198.51.100.20"}\n' "$ADMIN" "$n" "$n" > "$D/04-assumerole-$n.json"
done
# (5) cloud data-plane exfil burst (AWS Transfer Family / DataSync / Secrets + Azure snapshot)
for api in CreateServer CreateUser StartTaskExecution CreateLocationS3 GetSecretValue BatchGetSecretValue; do
  printf '{"event_name":"%s","cloud_provider":"AWS","saml_subject":"%s","source_ip":"198.51.100.20"}\n' "$api" "$ADMIN" > "$D/05-aws-$api.json"
done
printf '{"event_name":"MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/SNAPSHOTS/WRITE","cloud_provider":"AZURE","caller_principal_id":"%s","target_subscription_id":"attacker-sub","home_subscription_id":"victim-sub","resource_id":"disk-01","source_ip":"198.51.100.20"}\n' "$ADMIN" > "$D/05-azure-snapshot.json"
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-016 telemetry emitted (Okta takeover + rogue IdP + cross-cloud AssumeRole + data-plane burst).'

input_variables.name: TARGET_ADMIN
input_variables.description: The compromised tech-admin identity that owns the whole causality chain (CGO) and is the shared join key across every plane.

expected_artifacts.description: An Okta MFA factor reset on a privileged account followed within minutes by a privileged admin-console sign-in for the same identity from a new device/geo.
An Okta system-log IdP-lifecycle create/activate event adding a federated identity provider with JIT/impersonation linking, by a recently-reset admin.

A burst of federated AssumeRoleWithSAML / AssumeRole calls into multiple AWS accounts and Azure subscriptions keyed on the same federated subject, followed by Transfer Family / DataSync / Secrets Manager / Azure snapshot data-plane APIs.

biocs.name: MP-016 AWS Data-Movement Service Abuse Burst
biocs.description: A single federated principal drives a burst across two or more AWS data-movement services in one window — Transfer Family server/user creation (CreateServer / CreateUser), DataSync task execution and S3 location creation (StartTaskExecution / CreateLocationS3), and Secrets Manager mass secret reads (GetSecretValue / BatchGetSecretValue). These are legitimate managed services abused to exfiltrate at scale rather than malware; the BIOC keys on the multi-service abuse shape under one identity, emitting the normalized actor so the Cloud App burst equi-joins the ITDR takeover on the shared identity. This is the exploit_impact leg of the chain.
biocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_provider = "AWS"
| filter event_name in ("CreateServer", "CreateUser", "StartTaskExecution", "CreateLocationS3", "GetSecretValue", "BatchGetSecretValue")
| alter normalized_actor = lowercase(coalesce(saml_subject, user_identity_arn))
| alter svc = if(event_source = "transfer.amazonaws.com", "transfer", if(event_source = "datasync.amazonaws.com", "datasync", if(event_source = "secretsmanager.amazonaws.com", "secrets", "other")))
| comp count() as api_calls, count_distinct(svc) as services_abused, count_distinct(event_name) as distinct_apis by normalized_actor, source_ip
| filter services_abused >= 2 and api_calls >= 10
| fields normalized_actor, services_abused, distinct_apis, api_calls, source_ip

abiocs.name: MP-016 Help-Desk MFA Reset Then Rapid Privileged Okta Sign-In
abiocs.description: A privileged Okta account experiences an MFA factor reset (help-desk / admin-driven) and then, within the same short window, a successful privileged admin-console sign-in for the SAME identity — the reset->sign-in lineage of an account takeover. The ABIOC anchors to the account's learned factor-reset cadence and sign-in device/geo baseline rather than any static IP list, and keys on the target admin identity (emitted as normalized_actor / causality_actor_primary_username) so the endpoint- and cloud-plane legs equi-join it. This is malicious signal 1 of the chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = okta_sso
| filter eventType in ("user.session.start", "user.authentication.sso", "user.mfa.factor.reset_all")
| alter normalized_actor = lowercase(coalesce(target_user_email, actor_alternate_id))
| alter is_reset = if(eventType = "user.mfa.factor.reset_all", 1, 0)
| alter is_privsignin = if(admin_console_access = true and auth_result = "SUCCESS", 1, 0)
| comp sum(is_reset) as resets, sum(is_privsignin) as priv_signins, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen, count_distinct(client_geo_country) as countries by normalized_actor
| alter reset_to_signin_seconds = last_seen - first_seen
| filter resets >= 1 and priv_signins >= 1 and reset_to_signin_seconds <= 1800
| fields normalized_actor, resets, priv_signins, countries, reset_to_signin_seconds
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-account factor-reset cadence + sign-in device/geo baseline -> an MFA reset immediately followed by a privileged admin-console sign-in for the same identity, anchored to that identity and emitted as causality_actor_primary_username (normalized_actor) so the Cloud App and cloud data-plane legs equi-join it across planes.

abiocs.name: MP-016 Rogue Federated Identity Provider Added With Impersonation
abiocs.description: A recently-compromised Okta admin creates or activates a NEW federated identity provider with JIT provisioning / automatic account-link (impersonation) enabled — a tenant-trust modification that lets the actor mint sessions impersonating arbitrary downstream users and survives a password/MFA reset of the original account. The ABIOC keys on the rarity of IdP-administration for this actor against its learned admin-action baseline, not on the raw event, and emits the same normalized_actor so it stitches to signal 1. This is the exposure_exploit persistence pivot and malicious signal 2 of the chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = okta_sso
| filter eventType in ("system.idp.lifecycle.create", "system.idp.lifecycle.activate", "system.idp.lifecycle.update")
| filter outcome_result = "SUCCESS"
| alter normalized_actor = lowercase(actor_alternate_id)
| alter impersonation_enabled = if(idp_jit_enabled = true or idp_account_link_action = "AUTO", 1, 0)
| comp count() as idp_changes, values(idp_display_name) as new_idps, sum(impersonation_enabled) as impersonation_flags by normalized_actor, client_ip_address
| filter idp_changes >= 1 and impersonation_flags >= 1
| fields normalized_actor, new_idps, idp_changes, impersonation_flags, client_ip_address
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-admin administrative-action baseline -> a rare IdP-lifecycle create/activate with JIT/impersonation linking by the just-taken-over admin, anchored to that identity and emitted as causality_actor_primary_username (normalized_actor) so it equi-joins the takeover and the downstream cross-cloud legs.

abiocs.name: MP-016 Federated SSO AssumeRole Burst Across Cloud Accounts
abiocs.description: A single federated subject performs a burst of SSO role assumptions — AssumeRoleWithSAML / AssumeRole / AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity — into multiple AWS accounts and Azure subscriptions in one window, the fan-out that follows a rogue-IdP add. The ABIOC anchors to the principal's learned cross-account SSO baseline and keys on the shared federated subject identity (normalized_actor) so the assumption burst equi-joins the identity-plane takeover. This is the shared_entity pivot and malicious signal 3 of the chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter event_name in ("AssumeRoleWithSAML", "AssumeRole", "AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity")
| filter cloud_provider in ("AWS", "AZURE")
| alter normalized_actor = lowercase(coalesce(saml_subject, principal_email, user_identity_arn))
| comp count() as role_assumptions, count_distinct(recipient_account_id) as accounts, count_distinct(assumed_role_arn) as roles, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by normalized_actor, source_ip
| alter burst_seconds = last_seen - first_seen
| filter role_assumptions >= 5 and accounts >= 2
| fields normalized_actor, role_assumptions, accounts, roles, burst_seconds, source_ip
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-principal cross-account SSO baseline -> a fan-out of federated role assumptions into >= 2 cloud accounts inside one window, anchored to the shared federated subject identity and emitted as causality_actor_primary_username (normalized_actor) so the cloud legs stitch to the ITDR takeover.

xql_queries.name: MP-016 Privileged Okta Factor Reset From Help-Desk Flow
xql_queries.query:
dataset = okta_sso
| filter eventType in ("user.mfa.factor.reset_all", "user.mfa.factor.deactivate", "system.mfa.factor.deactivate")
| filter target_admin_role = true
| alter normalized_actor = lowercase(target_user_email)
| comp count() as reset_events, values(actor_alternate_id) as reset_by by normalized_actor, client_ip_address
| filter reset_events >= 1
| fields normalized_actor, reset_by, reset_events, client_ip_address

xql_queries.name: MP-016 Azure Managed-Disk Snapshot Copied To External Subscription
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_provider = "AZURE"
| filter event_name in ("MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/SNAPSHOTS/WRITE", "MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/DISKS/BEGINGETACCESS/ACTION", "MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/SNAPSHOTS/BEGINGETACCESS/ACTION")
| alter normalized_actor = lowercase(caller_principal_id)
| alter external_target = if(target_subscription_id != home_subscription_id, 1, 0)
| comp count() as snapshot_ops, sum(external_target) as external_copies, count_distinct(resource_id) as disks by normalized_actor, source_ip
| filter snapshot_ops >= 1 and external_copies >= 1
| fields normalized_actor, snapshot_ops, external_copies, disks, source_ip

xql_queries.name: MP-016 Cross-Cloud Takeover Stitched To One Identity
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| alter normalized_actor = lowercase(coalesce(saml_subject, caller_principal_id, user_identity_arn))
| comp count_distinct(cloud_provider) as clouds, count_distinct(event_name) as distinct_apis, count() as api_calls by normalized_actor
| filter clouds >= 1 and distinct_apis >= 3
| fields normalized_actor, clouds, distinct_apis, api_calls

correlation_rules.name: MP-016 Cross-Cloud Identity Takeover Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(MP-016 Help-Desk MFA Reset Then Rapid Privileged Okta Sign-In) AND ABIOC(MP-016 Rogue Federated Identity Provider Added With Impersonation) AND ABIOC(MP-016 Federated SSO AssumeRole Burst Across Cloud Accounts) AND (BIOC(MP-016 AWS Data-Movement Service Abuse Burst) OR XQL(MP-016 Azure Managed-Disk Snapshot Copied To External Subscription)), all joined on the shared normalized_actor identity key -- the compromised tech-admin, emitted as causality_actor_primary_username on every plane -- within a 3600s window. The legs fuse into ONE cross-cloud identity-takeover incident anchored to that identity's causality chain: help-desk MFA reset -> privileged Okta admin sign-in [ITDR] -> rogue federated IdP with impersonation added [Cloud App tenant-trust modification, the persistence pivot] -> federated SSO AssumeRole into AWS and Azure [shared_entity] -> Transfer Family / DataSync / Secrets Manager / Azure snapshot data-plane burst [exploit_impact]. The incident spans the ITDR and Cloud App planes and ranks critical; failure mode is four separate alerts when the window is missed or the shared identity key is not emitted on every plane.

use_cases.name: Muddled Libra Cross-Cloud Identity Takeover — Okta Admin to Rogue IdP to Data Exfil Stitch
use_cases.description: Prove Cortex XSIAM stitches a help-desk-driven Okta admin takeover, a rogue federated-IdP persistence pivot, and a cross-cloud data-plane exfiltration burst into a single identity-anchored incident — the Muddled Libra cloud playbook — instead of surfacing four unranked, unrelated alerts across the ITDR and Cloud App planes.

test_cases.objective: The Okta admin takeover and rogue-IdP persistence fire as identity-plane ABIOCs anchored to the same compromised admin identity.
preconditions: Per-account factor-reset and admin-action baselines learned.
steps: Emit the help-desk MFA reset + privileged admin sign-in for the target admin.
Emit the rogue federated IdP create with JIT/impersonation by the same admin.
Observe both ABIOCs fire keyed on the shared normalized_actor.
success_criteria: ABIOC `MP-016 Help-Desk MFA Reset Then Rapid Privileged Okta Sign-In` fires.
ABIOC `MP-016 Rogue Federated Identity Provider Added With Impersonation` fires.

test_cases.objective: The cross-cloud SSO AssumeRole burst and cloud data-plane abuse fire on the same identity and stitch to the identity-plane takeover.
preconditions: Per-principal cross-account SSO + cloud-API baselines learned.
steps: Emit the federated AssumeRole burst into >= 2 AWS/Azure accounts.
Emit the AWS Transfer Family / DataSync / Secrets Manager burst and the Azure snapshot copy.
Observe the AssumeRole ABIOC, the AWS data-movement BIOC, and the Azure snapshot XQL fire.
success_criteria: ABIOC `MP-016 Federated SSO AssumeRole Burst Across Cloud Accounts` fires.
BIOC `MP-016 AWS Data-Movement Service Abuse Burst` fires.
XQL `MP-016 Azure Managed-Disk Snapshot Copied To External Subscription` returns the external-copy row.

test_cases.objective: The correlation rule fuses every leg into ONE cross-cloud incident spanning the ITDR and Cloud App planes, keyed on the shared identity.
preconditions: The signals from TC-MP-016A and TC-MP-016B are present inside the correlation window.
steps: Run CR-MP-0016 over the run window.
Confirm a single incident_id anchors all legs on the shared normalized_actor.
Confirm the incident's causality chain spans ITDR + Cloud App.
success_criteria: The incident's planes >= {ITDR, CLOUD_APP} keyed on one normalized_actor.
No leg surfaces as an independent, unstitched alert.

preventive_controls: Harden the help desk against MFA-reset social engineering: require video/callback identity proofing and manager approval before resetting factors on privileged accounts, and alert on any factor reset for an admin-role identity.

Restrict IdP-administration in Okta to a tiny break-glass admin set with phishing-resistant MFA, and require change-management approval to add or activate a federated identity provider so a rogue IdP cannot be added silently.

Scope and monitor SSO-federated cloud roles: constrain AssumeRoleWithSAML trust policies, enforce permission boundaries on federated roles, and require just-in-time elevation for data-movement services (Transfer Family, DataSync, Secrets Manager) and snapshot/disk-export operations.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-account factor-reset cadence, admin-action rarity, and per-principal cloud-API baselines rather than hand-authoring static rules per event or per IP.

Emit a shared normalized identity key (causality_actor_primary_username) on the Okta, AWS, and Azure legs so the takeover, the rogue-IdP add, and the cross-cloud data-plane burst stitch into one incident within the correlation window.

Alert specifically on the rogue-IdP signature — a new federated IdP with JIT/impersonation linking added by a recently-reset admin — as the durable persistence pivot that survives an original-account reset.
